app_caption: Quality Control Protocol for Avaatech XRF Core Scanner
upload_info: Upload the Avaatech data file to start the QC.
strict_missing_help: When enabled (default), a row missing Throughput, Rh-Lα, or Rh-Lα-Inc has its Quality Index (QI) marked as indeterminate. When disabled, the QI is recalculated using only the available modules, redistributing the weights. In both modes the row is still flagged as indeterminate (QF=ND) — never as OK.
combine_rolling_label: Combine the 3 variables in Rolling QC (QC4)
combine_rolling_help: When disabled (default), QC4 only considers Rh-Lα-Inc — the actual spectral data measured; Throughput and Rh-Lα are secondary instrumental parameters. When enabled, it uses the largest drift deviation (|z-score|) among Throughput, Rh-Lα, and Rh-Lα-Inc — a physical measurement issue (crack, air gap, dry/wet transition) tends to show up in at least one of the three, widening sensitivity.
include_pca_qf_label: Include PCA in the QF criterion
include_pca_qf_help: When disabled (default), PCA (QC6) is always calculated and shown normally in the diagnostic tab, but does not contribute to the QI or QF — it stays purely exploratory. When enabled, the Mahalanobis distance contributes to the QI again (5% weight) and can trigger QF=2/3 on multivariate outliers.
use_count_mode_label: QF mode by module count (v4.2 protocol)
use_count_mode_help: When disabled (default), the QF is set by the weighted Quality Index (QI) — a very good module can compensate for a bad one. When enabled, uses the alternative criterion from the v4.2 protocol: each QC module becomes an OK/ALERT/CRITICAL state (its own thresholds, distinct from the QI mode), and the final QF is a non-compensatory count — QF1 = 1 ALERT, QF2 = 2-3 ALERTs or 1 CRITICAL, QF3 = 2+ CRITICALs or 4+ ALERTs. The QI is still calculated and shown normally in both modes — only the criterion deciding the QF changes. Rows with missing critical data remain flagged as indeterminate (QF=ND) in both modes.
depth_display_help: Chooses which depth column to use on the X axis of the charts, in the table, and in the PDF report. CompositeDepth (default) is continuous across the whole core; CoreDepth is local and resets at each sampling section/tube. Does not affect any QC calculation — display only. For multi-section cores, choosing CoreDepth may make charts and intervals look discontinuous at section boundaries.
pca_skipped_info: PCA (QC6) could not be computed for this file — insufficient elements or rows. The other QC modules are not affected.
pointwise_flag_note: ⚠ Triggered by a specific criterion ({causes}), not by the aggregate QI (QI={qi:.1f}).
pdf_pointwise_footnote: ⚠ Marked interval(s) were triggered by a specific criterion (z-score or Mahalanobis), not by the aggregate QI — QI remains in an acceptable range (≥{threshold}).

check.pca_unavailable: PCA (QC6) cannot be computed: only {n} of the {min} minimum required elements are present in the file. Score_PCA will default to a neutral value (100); the other QC modules continue normally.
check.pca_too_few_rows: PCA (QC6) cannot be computed: only {n} Rep0 row(s) found (minimum required: {min}). Score_PCA will default to a neutral value (100); the other QC modules continue normally.
check.zero_throughput: {n} rows with zero or null Throughput.
